overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation. Evidence could not show a quorum viewed the Google Drive draft, and a subquorum share of another draft was not deliberation. The AG voiced concern about the Drive use and reminded the Committee of serial-communication limits.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a quorum deliberated outside a posted meeting by drafting and circulating a response to a union no-confidence vote, including a shared Google Drive draft.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we are constrained to find that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law by deliberating outside of a properly posted meeting.

allegations.summary: Whether a member's individually drafted statement, shared with two other members, was deliberation among a quorum.
allegations.key_passage: We do not find that the Committee deliberated outside of a meeting with respect to Mr. Stein’s statement as his statement was shared with only two Committee members prior to the June 21, 2024, meeting.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
